summary: Apocrypha 1.0 is the browser-delivered web/PWA release for responsive desktop, iOS, and Android surfaces. The exact candidate passed local automated desktop Chrome, Pixel-class Chrome, and iPhone 15 Pro WebKit checks covering owner access, manifest identity, service-worker scope, offline encrypted continuity, no private API caching, accessibility, safe areas, and overflow. No downloadable native binary is part of this release, and this record does not claim App Store or Play Store packaging, physical-device verification, phone-to-desktop live acceptance, or production deployment.

plan.objective: Keep Apocrypha useful, local, private, evidence-linked, and quietly alive between prompts while every external effect remains governed.
principles: Local operation remains useful when network access is removed.
Memory, claims, and actions retain source and authority boundaries.
Unavailable capabilities remain visibly degraded instead of simulated.
Public distribution waits for integrity, signature, install, rollback, and privacy proof.

milestones.label: 1.0 cross-platform web/PWA
milestones.summary: Version 1.0.0 is an installable browser-delivered PWA release. The local automated matrix passed desktop Chrome, Pixel-class Chrome, and iPhone 15 Pro WebKit checks for access, manifest identity, service-worker scope, offline encrypted continuity, private-cache exclusion, accessibility, safe areas, and overflow. No App Store, Play Store, desktop-native, or downloadable package is claimed; production deployment and physical-device verification remain separate operational acceptance gates.

milestones.label: Personal Brain
milestones.summary: The simplified public shell, owner gate, and row-secured Mneme schema are live. Candidate 6 adds an explicit, authenticated, idempotent first-owner bootstrap instead of creating a profile silently; live owner creation and readback remain acceptance gates.

milestones.label: Mobile mini Brain and desktop sync
milestones.summary: The 1.0 PWA release includes an AES-GCM device-local vault, deterministic no-model recall and refusal, an installable offline shell, signed cursor and outbox synchronization, replay and conflict controls, and a restricted desktop relay. Desktop Chrome, Pixel-class Chrome, and iPhone 15 Pro WebKit checks passed in local automation; no physical-phone or end-to-end phone-to-desktop verification is claimed.

milestones.label: Conversation constellations
milestones.summary: A privacy-safe aggregate exposes corpus scale and curated constellations without publishing raw conversation bodies; every held record remains unavailable until individual review and approval.

milestones.label: Humanity source admission
milestones.summary: A digest-bound admission gate separates reputation, factual trust, and human value while quarantining testimony and rejecting prohibited material.

milestones.label: Causal interoception and recovery
milestones.summary: Redacted causal traces, stable errors, stage latency fields, differential backups, and restore verification are implemented in the compatibility runtime.

milestones.label: CSL, NIL, and CSSL native core
milestones.summary: CSLv3 defines the contract, NIL defines the ordered timing graph, and CSSLv3 is the compiled target. The hardened native context frame is 1,780 tokenizer tokens, but the first canary exposed missing child-exit evidence; semantic parity, executable CSSLv3 policy, latency, and stable canary gates remain open.

milestones.label: Own executable language stack
milestones.summary: An authored artifact must change bounded behavior through a verified compiler or runtime to count. The first proofs are context selection, Graphify traversal, and mobile reconciliation under one inspectable NIL trace, with plain-language CSLv3 expansion and rollback.

milestones.label: Trinity-native cognitive organs
milestones.summary: Graphify is the first differential replacement. A read-only Rust query and path slice preserved exact fixed-query results, retained the Python oracle's morphology results, reduced cold-start cost, and proved that a sealed CSSLv3 policy changes bounded traversal while emitting a non-authoritative NIL trace. Product integration and a self-hosted CSSLv3 compiler remain open.

milestones.label: Signed local distribution
milestones.summary: A reversible Windows migration package exists and passed focused checks, but remains withheld pending native cryptographic signing, SBOM, and clean-machine lifecycle proof.

plan.release_boundary: This plan is the public-safe 1.0 web/PWA release record. It is not a deployment receipt, production acceptance result, native-app claim, or physical-device verification.

changelog.summary: The local-living architecture became the active build direction with local-first, privacy, authority, and rollback constraints.
The private Brain gained persistent-conversation seams plus graph, timeline, and source-tunnel memory views.
Humanity source admission now fails closed before memory and preserves difficult testimony only as attributed quarantine evidence.
The same worldline admitted and answered an exact live continuity turn after the settled-history hot loop was removed from the one-second heartbeat.
The compatibility runtime gained causal stage traces, stable error codes, bounded telemetry, differential backups, and verified restore semantics.

The migration contract now binds CSLv3 semantics, a NIL timing graph, CSSLv3 compiled kernels, and meet-or-exceed promotion gates; the first deterministic Rust context shadow passed its focused tests and microbenchmark.
The simplified Apocky home, owner-gated Apocrypha route, Atlas, conversation constellations, and new icon family were promoted and exercised across desktop, Pixel, and iPhone viewports.
The corpus prototype reports 1,386 held conversations and 19,479 messages through aggregate and curated projections while raw bodies and unreviewed detail remain unpublished.
Muted text contrast was raised and the live conversation surface passed accessibility and overflow checks on desktop, Pixel, and iPhone viewports.
A reversible Windows migration package was built and verified locally; no public download is exposed until native signature and lifecycle gates pass.
The public aggregate is now generated deterministically from sealed privacy-safe facts during every build; both live projections are byte-identical and all 1,386 records remain review-held.

A real mobile visit exposed a missing Mneme schema. The four storage tables and thirteen owner/service policies are now live with row-level security and zero anonymous-visible rows; owner bootstrap and signed two-device synchronization remain unproven.

The native migration now covers cognitive organs themselves: Graphify first, then shared traversal, provenance, scheduling, memory, diagnostics, MCP, API, and TTY kernels, with Python retained only as a frozen differential oracle until superseded.

CSLv3 contracts, NIL graphs, and CSSLv3 kernels now have an execution gate: embedded, displayed, or hashed language artifacts do not count until they produce a measured behavioral change through the language runtime.

The private Mneme substrate now exposes four row-secured tables and thirteen policies; anonymous boundary probes see no rows. Authenticated owner registration and phone-to-desktop data flow remain separate gates.
The candidate 5 cutover was retained. Repeated probes now resolve the canonical and bare-domain Apocrypha routes plus plan, changelog, and manifest without rolling back.

The missing first-owner path now has an explicit Mneme bootstrap, and the mobile surface has an encrypted local vault, deterministic offline reflection, signed replay-safe synchronization, conflict preservation, and a no-API-cache service worker. Physical-phone and live desktop synchronization remain acceptance gates.

The first Trinity organ now executes a sealed CSSLv3 query policy through a bounded native runtime and emits an inspectable non-authoritative NIL trace. Exact fixed-query parity, morphology retention, policy countertests, startup latency, and rollback were measured; product integration remains open.

The 1.0.0 browser-delivered web/PWA release has one route-aware install manifest, iOS safe-area activation, an unobscured telemetry-blackout surface, strict private-response no-store behavior, no private API entries in service-worker caches, offline encrypted restart coverage, serious and critical accessibility checks, and narrow-screen overflow checks across local automated desktop Chrome, Pixel-class Chrome, and iPhone 15 Pro WebKit. Native binaries, physical-device verification, and production deployment are not claimed.

Saved messages remain encrypted on the device while a delayed reply is pending. Retry preserves the original message, reconnecting resumes its delivery, and changing accounts cannot send another account’s pending text. Conversation history is retained across the service restart.
Assistant replies display readable headings, lists, emphasis and code through an escaped renderer. The saved message text, copy actions, history and pending delivery are preserved.
